en: Water lilies in local ponds have wide, waxy leaves that float to capture maximum sunlight.
Male frogs croak loudly during the rainy season to attract female mates for breeding.
Sweat cools the human body down because the evaporation of water from the skin absorbs heat.
Mangrove trees grow dense, stilt-like roots in coastal mud to survive strong ocean waves.
The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that allow it to hunt insects in dark forests.
Hermaphroditic papaya trees produce flowers containing both male and female parts to self-pollinate and bear fruit.
Weaver ants build nests in mango trees by weaving leaves together using larval silk.
The human tongue detects five basic tastes, including sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami.
Aloe vera plants store water in their thick, fleshy leaves to survive dry garden periods.
Mudskippers use their strong front fins to walk on coastal mudflats and breathe air.
Mosquitoes lay eggs in stagnant water, where they hatch into wiggling larvae called wrigglers.
Epiphytic orchids grow on high tree branches in the forest to access more sunlight.
